text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1% today to $142.34, extending a remarkable two-week rally of nearly 14%. The stock has climbed steadily as oil prices have surged on Middle East tensions—specifically Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and reported strikes on Saudi Arabian oil facilities. These supply disruption fears have pushed crude prices sharply higher, with world oil trading at $125 per barrel (versus $96 domestically), directly benefiting major oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The broader backdrop is one of heightened geopolitical risk in a key global oil chokepoint. While today's news showed some pullback in oil prices as traders digested fresh data, the underlying tension—Iran's escalating campaign against shipping and energy infrastructure—remains unresolved, keeping the market on edge and supporting elevated crude valuations that favor upstream producers.
